name: Krestauros
body:
Krestauros
CR 7

These magnificent bulls are paragons of the bovine form, sleek and perfect in fetlock and flank, with hides that glisten in perfect silver-gray, snow-white, or burnished gold.

XP 3,200
N Large magical beast
Init +5; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +15; Aura illuck, majesty (DC 17)

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 10, flat-footed 19 (+1 Dex, +10 natural, -1 size)
hp 83 (9d10+45)
Fort +10, Ref +7, Will +6
Defensive Abilities Death Curse, divine resilience

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee gore +13 (2d6+5), 2 hooves +8 (1d6+2)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks bellow, destructive, powerful charge (gore, 4d6+7), wild momentum

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 12, Con 19, Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 16
Base Atk +9; CMB +15; CMD 26 (30 vs. trip)
Feats Endurance, Improved Initiative, Improved Natural Attack (gore), Power Attack, Toughness
Skills Perception +15, Swim+17
Languages Common (cannot speak)
SQ command

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bellow (Su)

Three times per day, the krestauros can bellow, causing all creatures within 30 feet of the krestauros to make a DC 17 Will saving throw. Those who fail are frightened of the krestauros.

A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is unaffected. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Command (Su)

The krestauros can issue a command to a creature that is fascinated by its majesty ability. The creature then follows the command on its next turn. The krestauros can only command a creature to grapple or bull rush another creature, perform the aid another action on the krestauros, or to move up to its movement speed in a direction decided by the krestauros.

Death Curse (Su)

If a krestauros is slain, any creature that dealt damage to it within the previous 1 minute must make a DC 17 Will saving throw or be afflicted with a random curse (as the bestow curse spell) lasting 24 hours. Each dawn thereafter, a cursed creature can attempt a new saving throw to end the curse.

If the cursed creature fails three saving throws in a row, the curse becomes permanent. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Destructive (Ex)

A krestauros deals double damage to objects and structures with its attacks.

Divine Resilience (Su)

Three times a day, a krestauros can choose to reroll a saving throw that it has failed. It must accept the second result. This ability can only be used on a specific saving throw once.

Illuck Aura (Su)

All other creatures within 1 mile of the krestauros suffer from bad luck, taking a -1 penalty on all d20 rolls. In addition, whenever a creature rolls a natural 1, it is struck with a surge of bad fortune for 1 minute. During this time, their circumstance modifier increases to -3.

Majesty (Su)

A creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of the krestauros must make a DC 17 Will saving throw. On a failure, the creature is fascinated with the krestauros for 1 hour and cannot act against or harm the krestauros. An ally of the fascinated creature can use one action to shake the fascinated creature from its condition, allowing that creature to make another saving throw as a reaction. A creature that succeeds at its saving throw or frees itself from the fascination is immune to the krestauros’ aura of majesty for the next 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Wild Momentum (Ex)

A creature damaged from a krestauros’ powerful charge ability is knocked prone (DC 19 Reflex negates).

The save DC is Strength-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any hills or plains
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

These magnificent bulls are paragons of the bovine form, sleek and perfect in fetlock and flank, with hides that glisten in perfect silver-gray, snow-white, or burnished gold. These sacred animals were created by the gods as pleasing and perfect sacrifices, but their majestic appearance was so fine that the long ago kings for whom they were created kept back the krestauros for their own and gave back inferior beasts in sacrifice to the gods. In vengeance, the gods laid curses upon these feckless royals, bringing terror upon their houses with strange passions, monstrous births, and bouts of destruction across the land. Some of the krestauros were captured or slain by mighty heroes, but some still roam the land and tend to bring doom in their wake all unknowing.

The krestauros is not malicious and can sometimes be lured away from an area to remove its doom-bringing presence elsewhere, but striking down these blessed beasts may bring its own divine wrath upon their slayers.
